findings.failure_path: A list item beginning `-     example` uses one space of CommonMark list padding and four spaces of code indentation. The parser records a six-column content indent, so a later two-space fence in that item is treated as root-level. If the fence is unclosed, a following root obligation is swallowed and deleting it can yield zero derived rows. A fence that opens directly after a list marker is also missed because the opener is matched against the raw line.
findings.smallest_fix: Determine fence indentation from the CommonMark list content boundary, including padding after the marker and an opener on the marker line. Add deletion regressions for both forms.

findings.failure_path: The no-lazy-fetch test imports the helper and inspects its dictionary. M26 removes the assignment from that helper. The CLI fixture only reads complete local history, and the packet omits the revision-read call. These checks can stay green if the actual Git invocation drops the setting or a supported Git version ignores it.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the revision-read call in the packet and exercise the CLI with a missing promised blob and a test-owned remote. Assert the read error and zero fetch attempts on the oldest supported Git version.

findings.failure_path: The four added rows each have an owner and evidence fields. The packet omits the applicable item-9 and impact-chain gate logic and negative cases. A clean run on populated rows can also occur if the gate accepts a missing owner row, invalid evidence label, or missing firing path.
findings.smallest_fix: Attach the applicable predicates and candidate-bound negative results showing that each missing or invalid field blocks the landing gate.

findings.failure_path: Register row 921 claims RED-baseline evidence for the ledger-scope correction, but T2 records parser and Git failures plus a passing text check. The text checks remain green if Step 6 keeps its pointer and drops the requirement to persist origin, pre-draft source IDs, and observations. The packet also omits the Decision Persistence section needed to verify the destination.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the Decision Persistence section and record a paired narrow-backend replay in which temporary-only evidence reaches closeout on the baseline and is rejected by the candidate.

findings.failure_path: The revised 213/213 count carries forward a claim of exact carrier and governing-heading verification. The packet omits the revised preservation rows and the destination excerpts needed to resolve earlier mismatches, including the database trigger previously mapped to the file title and the minimum pressure set previously mapped to a heading alone. The aggregate can stay green while those obligations point to text that does not enforce them.
findings.smallest_fix: Attach the regenerated rows and numbered destination excerpts for the disputed carriers. Verify the operative text and governing heading for each before retaining the exact-verification claim.

The Git fixture protects setup from caller HOME and XDG configuration. Its revision read uses existing blobs, leaving the missing-object exit path unverified.

The shown changes require no data migration or staged rollout. The validation ledger leaves boundary acceptance pending.

The profile reports both script-contract leak suites at the frozen revision. The durable-ledger behavior change still lacks the reproducible failing baseline required by the root contract.
